applied.problem: The opening definition and bold summary say the slope comes from the quantity itself, but dy/dt = 2t in this lesson uses time, and the second-order equations of i5 to i7 give a rate of a rate and need two starting values, so the summary must say first-order.

"Each minute it loses a tenth of its gap" reads the rate as an amount over a minute; over a whole minute the gap shrinks by about 9.5%, not 10%, the very mistake the practice warns against and one i2 and i4 will expose.

"Set the rate to zero and solve. It is a flat line" only works when the rate depends on the quantity alone; for dy/dt = 2t it gives t = 0, which the mistakes list itself says is not a steady state, and some rules have none.
